# List

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:list` · Kerf UI · component · Navigation

A vertical stack with physical-axis alignment, side-selectable text/control insets, optional typed token/length gap, flex growth, vertical scrolling, and independently selectable divider edges.

## When to use

Standardize vertical component layout, optional physical-side text/control insets, and scroll/divider ownership instead of repeating ad-hoc flex-column wrappers.

- Arrange component rows or sections in a vertical stretch-aligned stack.
- Let one bounded list own vertical scrolling, flex growth, or one or more physical-edge dividers.
- Choose a finite gap shorthand such as xs or m, or compose a typed length with @kerfjs/ui/css-values when the spacing scale is insufficient.
- Use a finite flex keyword or the flex() builder when List participates in flexible layout.
- Apply the standard text or control inset to selected physical sides without an application wrapper.
- Align children horizontally or distribute them vertically with the same physical alignment vocabulary as Row.
- Use selectionMode="multiple" and ariaLabel to group selectable rich ContentItem rows in a multi-select grid.
- Use scrollClearance on the scrollable List that reaches an edge overlaid by chrome (a DialogSurface floating footer) so rows scroll visibly beneath it while the first and last rows still rest clear of it.
- Render a bounded, framed result picker of ListItem rows (search results, duplicate candidates) with scrollable, frame, and typed maxHeight/minHeight instead of an app-owned bordered scroller.

**Not when:**

- Do not use List as semantic list markup; use ul/ol when list semantics are required and apply layout deliberately.
- Do not create nested scroll owners or use divider sides as a substitute for meaningful grouping.
- Do not pass raw CSS strings to gap or flex, mix their distinct grammars, or use the off-rhythm s/xl spacing steps without a deliberate exception.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/list` — exports `List`.
- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/css-values` — exports `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `plus`, `calc`, `flex`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/list` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/list.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Wiring: `wireScrollDividers` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-scroll-dividers` (optional).
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/list`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuilist), [`@kerfjs/ui/css-values`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuicss-values), [`@kerfjs/ui/wire-scroll-dividers`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuiwire-scroll-dividers) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- no gap
- standard boolean gap
- named none/2xs/xs/s/m/l/xl token gap
- typed CssLength gap
- boolean, finite-keyword, or typed CssFlex flex
- scrollable
- scrollClearance block-start, block-end, or both: clears overlaying chrome inside the scroll area
- frame: 1px neutral border, control radius, and a 4px focus-ring-safe inset
- typed CssLength maxHeight and minHeight bounds
- base or raised solid surface
- document reading inset
- left/center/right/full horizontal alignment
- top/middle/bottom/full vertical alignment
- top/right/bottom/left divider combinations
- top/right/bottom/left text and control inset combinations
- fill: the layout root fills a definite-height parent
- rootAttributes: safe data-\*, aria-\*, and structural role on the root
- scroll dividers when named as wireScrollDividers targets chrome
- multi-select grid for rich ContentItem rows

**CSS-value props** (typed builders from `@kerfjs/ui/css-values`; raw CSS strings are rejected):

- `gap`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; shorthands `none`, `2xs`, `xs`, `m`, `l`; exceptional (justify) `s`, `xl`; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `gap="xs"`
- `flex`: flex grammar; raw values: forbid; shorthands `none`, `auto`, `initial`; helpers `flex` — e.g. `flex="none"`
- `maxHeight`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `maxHeight={rem(14)}`
- `minHeight`: length grammar; raw values: forbid; helpers `px`, `rem`, `em`, `pct`, `space`, `lengthVar`, `calc` — e.g. `minHeight={rem(4.25)}`

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`, `navigation-list`, `vertical-layout`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [ListHeader](./list-header.md), [ListActionRow](./list-action-row.md), [ListItem](./list-item.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** child semantics and content; the bounded height needed for scrolling; typed gap, flex, alignment, and divider choices; the accessible label and selection state of a multi-select grid; which one scroller opts into scroll clearance (the one reaching the covered edge); the result picker bounds (maxHeight/minHeight) and its rows.

**Wiring:** `wireScrollDividers` is optional.

**Wiring-owned state attributes** — never render, remove, or branch on these as app state:

- `data-scroll-overflow` on `the targets scroller` (`wireScrollDividers`): The physical edges, in canonical t/r/b/l order, beyond which content is scrolled out of view; absent when nothing is hidden (content that fits never reports its far edges). Re-applied if a re-render drops it.
- `data-scroll-divider` on `a List named as targets chrome` (`wireScrollDividers`): The sides, in t/r/b/l order, on which this chrome currently draws its scroll divider: the side facing the scroller while content is hidden beyond it. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.
- `data-header-overlay` on `kui-pane` (`wireScrollDividers`): measured once the wiring has measured a Pane's overlay header (headerPresentation: overlay) and published its border-box height as --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start on the Pane root, plus a classic content scrollbar's inline size as --kui-pane-scrollbar-inline-size, which the header leaves uncovered. Re-applied if a re-render drops it.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: conditional · padding: conditional (layout role: navigation). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- List adds no margin. dividerSides draws selected physical edges without changing geometry; textInsets adds the full 17px content inset and controlInsets adds 8px on selected sides, with text winning on overlap.
- scrollClearance adds the inherited --kui-scroll-clearance-block-start/end context, published by overlaying chrome, to the List block padding and scroll-padding on the opted-in edges; without it the context is ignored.
- frame draws a 1px --kui-color-neutral-border-normal border with --kui-radius-m and a 4px --kui-space-2xs inset on every side (replacing inset/textInsets/controlInsets), exactly the focus-ring reach, so the first and last rows' rings stay inside the clip at the scroll extremes; maxHeight/minHeight bound the List directly.
- Every scrollable List's block scroll padding is the focus-ring reach plus 2px of slack (6px, no change at rest), so any row focused or scrolled into view stops with its ring inside the clip; an unframed List's first and last rows still meet the clip at the scroll extremes, so use frame when they must show a whole ring.
- As a direct child of a Pane's scrolling content, a List that does not scroll itself never shrinks below its rows (flex-shrink 0), so the content's block-end padding (a bottom safe area, an overlay NavStack bottom toolbar's clearance) follows its last row.

## Accessibility

- List adds layout only and no list role by default; selectionMode="multiple" makes it an aria-multiselectable grid with a required ariaLabel for selectable ContentItem rows.
- Give a scrollable List a bounded block size and keep keyboard focus visible as its contents scroll.
- A focused scrollable List (a keyboard-focusable scroller) draws the theme focus ring inset and rounded inside its own box, so a rounded or clipping parent never cuts it off; do not restyle its focus.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-list`.

Never put `kui-list` on an element you write; render `List` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Public tokens it reads: `--kui-color-neutral-border-normal`, `--kui-color-surface`, `--kui-color-surface-raised`, `--kui-layout-item-gap`, `--kui-list-divider-color`, `--kui-list-gap`, `--kui-space-l`, `--kui-space-m`, `--kui-space-xl`. Set a token only where its public contract allows; prefer a prop.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
